h: Shabbos Awakens Gentle Teshuvah That Can Endure Forever

p: In the Minchah prayer we mention
"On the day Hashem gives you rest
from your sorrow and from your trembling."
is the root of the evil inclination,
(דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ד, י) לְבִלְתִּי עׇצְבִּי
"'That it not grieve me' (Divrei HaYamim I 4:10)
that the evil inclination not overpower me
the agitation of the evil inclination,
his good inclination against the evil inclination."
And this pasuk is expounded in the holy Zohar
as referring to the day of Shabbos,
which is "the day He gives rest,"
repose into the heart of Yisrael.
And likewise is the matter of
what is mentioned in the Megillah
after the wiping out of Amalek:
"And they had rest from their enemies" (Esther 9:16);
for Amalek is the root of the evil inclination,
and after they merited the wiping out of Amalek
"and they had rest from their enemies."
after the day of Shabbos has passed in keeping,
then one merits rest from the evil inclination.
And in the holy Zohar (this parsha, III 85b):
"And just as the Holy One, blessed be He,
so should a person learn, etc."
if he is a person who would be ashamed,
he should not say it to him
like one speaking of other matters, etc."
And this needs to be understood:
that at first He rebukes him in private;
so from where does it learn
that even in private one should not rebuke him,
but only as though telling about others?
הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ מְדַבֵּר עִם הָאָדָם
Hashem Yisbarach does not speak with a person
only by sending into his heart
and it seems to the person
that he of himself was awakened to teshuvah.
And this is mainly on Shabbos,
when an awakening to teshuvah comes to a person.
that a person too should not rebuke his fellow
but should bring it about that he awakens of himself
by telling before him about others.
make it known to him among his loved ones, etc.,
at the time when the High Priest, etc."
And now that there is no impurity of afflictions,
it is that He puts it into the hearts of others
this too is from Hashem Yisbarach;
and this is "make it known to him among his loved ones."
And this is what is said in the psalm of Shabbos:
"It is good to give thanks (lehodos) to Hashem";
"He who confesses and forsakes will be shown mercy";
for on Shabbos a person is aroused to teshuvah,
And before this prayer we say (Tehillim 69:14):
"And as for me, my prayer, etc.,
answer me with the truth of Your salvation";
in the manner of what they said
and we ask that the salvation be in truth,
which is "the lip of truth is established forever":
that the thought of teshuvah widen
until he returns in complete teshuvah,
to confess and forsake in truth.
וְזֶה זוֹכִין בִּסְעוּדָה זוֹ שֶׁל יַעֲקֹב
And this one merits at this meal of Yaakov,
whose attribute is the attribute of truth:
that "the lip of truth be established forever."
